Verdict: **(B) return a material improvement to D0.**

The note is not stated over the published Bojinov–Simchi-Levi–Zhao class. Their 2023 paper assumes fixed nonanticipating potential outcomes, a known exact \(m\)-period carryover horizon, bounded outcomes, and precommitted “regular switchback” designs generated by independent coin flips at fixed randomization points. It optimizes the squared-error risk of their Horvitz–Thompson estimator for
\[
\tau_m=(T-m)^{-1}\sum_{t=m+1}^T\{Y_t(\mathbf1_{m+1})-Y_t(\mathbf0_{m+1})\},
\]
not over arbitrary estimators or outcome-adaptive policies. The note instead uses soft polynomial memory, the all-time sustained-policy GATE, arbitrary estimators, and all sequential kernels.

There is a useful outcome-class inclusion:
\[
\mathcal C_m(B)\subseteq\mathcal P_{T,\beta}\!\left(B,\,2B(1+m)^{1+\beta}\right),
\]
where \(\mathcal C_m(B)\) is the bounded exact-\(m\) class. Thus a genuine arbitrary-estimator, all-policy converse on a suitable finite-\(m\) subclass would transfer upward to the note’s class. But Bojinov et al.’s minimax result is only over regular designs for their fixed HT procedure, so it is not that converse. Their regular fixed-epoch construction can improve the auxiliary variance constant asymptotically from \(8e-4\approx17.75\) toward \(16\), but this is secondary and does not change the rate.

The material missed improvement is the radius-aware oracle scale and its elbows. The existing `lem:markov-upper-audit` already implies minimization over \(b\):
\[
R_T^{(2)}
 \le \min_{1\le b\le T}
 \left\{B\sqrt{(8e-4)b/T}+\frac{2eC}{\beta}(b+1)^{-\beta}\right\}^{2}
 \wedge 4B^2.
\]
The interior scale is
\[
b_\star\asymp_\beta\left\{(C/B)^2T\right\}^{1/(2\beta+1)},
\]
clipped to \([1,T]\), not merely \(T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\). This exposes three finite-horizon regimes:

\[
\begin{cases}
B^2/T, & C/B\lesssim T^{-1/2},\\
B^{4\beta/(2\beta+1)}C^{2/(2\beta+1)}
T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)},&
T^{-1/2}\lesssim C/B\lesssim T^\beta,\\
B^2,& C/B\gtrsim T^\beta.
\end{cases}
\]

The open certificate is also nonmaximal in its radius dependence. Its memory obstruction should be
\[
B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta},
\]
rather than \((B\wedge C)^2L^{-2\beta}\); bounded transports cap the perturbation after scaling, not before it. The present expression loses the high-memory elbow.

For `oeq:sequential-multiscale-certificate`, a no-log result is not ruled out, but it is not reachable from the current single-scale dichotomy. Arbitrary mixtures of run lengths can spread their useful mass over \(\Theta(\log L)\) dyadic bands. Removing that factor would require a genuinely new simultaneous multiscale prior or a square-function/Carleson-type occupancy inequality. With the frozen handle, the honest strongest immediate objective is a policy-uniform log-loss certificate and hence a two-sided bracket
\[
c_\beta\,
\max\!\left\{\frac{B^2}{T},
\frac{1}{\log(eT)}
\min\!\left[B^2,\,
B^{4\beta/(2\beta+1)}C^{2/(2\beta+1)}
T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}
\right]\right\}
\le R_T^{(2)}
\]
against the radius-aware upper bound above. The no-log frontier should remain a secondary open strengthening unless D0 supplies the new multiscale inequality. The log lower bound is not yet proved in the discharged note, so it must not be promoted to a theorem without that proof.

The likelihood defect is repairable without changing the common-null kernel or any prior. The object currently called \(q_{\mathsf Q}(y\mid w)\) must not be the observational conditional density of \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\) given \(W=w\). Define instead the structural/interventional path law
\[
\mu_{\mathsf Q}^{\,w}
 =\operatorname{Law}_{\mathsf Q}\!\left(
   Y_1(w_1),\ldots,Y_T(w_{1:T})
 \right),
\qquad
\ell_{\mathsf Q}(y;w)
 =\frac{d\mu_{\mathsf Q}^{\,w}}{d\lambda^T}(y).
\]
Then, against counting measure in \(w\) and \(\lambda^T\) in \(y\),
\[
p_{\mathsf Q,\pi}(w,y)
=
\left\{\prod_{t=1}^T
 \pi_t(w_t\mid w_{1:t-1},y_{1:t-1})\right\}
\ell_{\mathsf Q}(y;w).
\]
The actual observational conditional density is proportional to this product and generally is not \(\ell_{\mathsf Q}(y;w)\). In the joint-law Radon–Nikodym ratio, however, the common assignment factor cancels:
\[
\frac{dP_{\mathsf Q,\pi}}{dP_{\mathsf Q_0,\pi}}(w,y)
=
\frac{\ell_{\mathsf Q}(y;w)}
     {\ell_{\mathsf Q_0}(y;w)}
\]
on the common support. This remains valid for outcome-adaptive and deterministic kernels because the kernel factor is the same measurable function of \((w,y)\) under every prior. The endpoint-preserving transports already give common structural support. The most credible lower-bound re-derivation is a randomized-offset dyadic stopping-time/Carleson construction, not another global single-scale run-length dichotomy. For each length-\(L\) macroblock, build its dyadic interval tree. At a monochromatic node, use the opposite-arm block sign and its exact posterior-variance payoff. At a mixed node, descend to the first scale at which the two child histories separate and charge that node to the corresponding arm-specific band transport. Use lag bands \([b,2b)\), so different levels consume disjoint coordinates of the polynomial sensitivity envelope. Randomize the offset inside each candidate prior, then select a level from the known policy’s expectation under the common null before assignment.

The required new deterministic lemma should be formulated directly in the posterior-variance/information quantities generated by those priors:

\[
\mathsf{PV}^{\mathrm{blk}}_{L}(w)
+
\sum_{j=0}^{\lceil\log_2L\rceil}
\sum_{a=0}^{1}
\mathsf{CR}_{2^j,a}(w)
\ge c_\beta
\min\!\left\{\frac{B^2L}{T},
              B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta}\right\}.
\]

Here \(\mathsf{PV}^{\mathrm{blk}}_L\) must be the normalized conditional posterior variance from unresolved block-arm signs, and \(\mathsf{CR}_{b,a}\) must be the actual constrained-risk payoff—endpoint separation squared minus its rigorously bounded structural \(\chi^2\), Hellinger, or KL information—not merely an informal positive-part “energy.” Prove the inequality by charging every macroblock once at its first mixed dyadic node. After expectation under the common-null path law, one of the \(O(\log L)\) candidates then yields
\[
\inf_{\widehat\theta}
\mathbb E_{Q_{\pi,L},\pi}
[(\widehat\theta-\theta_T)^2]
\ge
\frac{\kappa_\beta}{\log(eL)}
\min\!\left\{\frac{B^2L}{T},
              B^2\wedge C^2L^{-2\beta}\right\}.
\]
This construction is materially different from the failed attempt: it assigns each mixed macroblock at its first separating tree node and works with genuine posterior/constrained-risk payoffs; it does not require one global run-length scale to classify an arbitrary concatenated path.
